request_classification.request_type: documentation-wide terminology refactor with governance constraints

claims.claim_text: Replace 'Layer 2' and 'Layer-2' with 'truth_store' across all files under Documentation/ and CLAUDE.md, where the terms refer to the project's architectural layers.
claims.classification_rationale: The terms 'Layer 2' and 'Layer-2' are pervasive current-state terminology throughout the canonical documentation set. CLAUDE.md Section 3.1 explicitly defines 'Layer 2' as 'operational at snapshot boundary' — a current-state architectural description. Renaming this term constitutes a contract-affecting documentation change to current-state truth. The term appears in CLAUDE.md Sections 1, 3, 4, 11, and throughout the canonical v1 document set. This is not a target-state or historical claim — it proposes changing how existing, currently-documented architecture is named.
notes: This is a current-state documentation modification, not a claim about new implementation
Touches the constitutional document (CLAUDE.md) directly — highest governance sensitivity
Layer 2 is described as 'complete at contract boundary' (Phase A) — renaming affects phase-gate language

claims.claim_text: Replace 'Layer 3' and 'Layer-3' with 'decision_layer' across all files under Documentation/ and CLAUDE.md, where the terms refer to the project's architectural layers.
claims.classification_rationale: The term 'Layer 3' has dual scope in canonical documentation. In CLAUDE.md Section 3.2, Layer 3 components (Feature Builder, Index Suite, Regime Gate, etc.) are explicitly 'planned only' — target-state. However, Layer 3 is also referenced in current-state documentation as an architectural boundary concept: CLAUDE.md Section 4 (Phase B: 'allowed, not completed'), Section 6.1 ('Layer 3+ MUST read ONLY from published snapshots'), and the snapshot contract. The term itself is part of current documentation truth even though the layer's implementation is target-state. Renaming it is a current-state documentation change that touches both current truth (the boundary/contract language) and target architecture (the planned components).
notes: Layer 3 references span current-state rules (snapshot contract, phase gates) and target-state components
CLAUDE.md Section 3.2 explicitly lists Layer-3 components as 'planned only'
The existing layer2/index_suite.py is called out in CLAUDE.md Section 3.2 as distinct from the planned Layer-3 Index Suite — rename must preserve this distinction
Phase B ('Layer 3 Bootstrap — allowed, not completed') and Phase C ('Layer 3 Structured Buildout — future') would need term adaptation

claims.claim_text: Enforce the rename as a strict naming convention only where terms refer to the project's architectural layers, not blindly altering unrelated literals, code module names, import paths, or historical references.
claims.classification_rationale: This constraint aligns directly with multiple constitutional principles. CLAUDE.md Section 2.3 requires that historical documents outside the canonical set must not be used as current truth — implying historical references have a distinct preservation role. CLAUDE.md Section 2.4 requires role-matched interpretation. The request's insistence on context-aware replacement (architectural references only) is consistent with the project's evidence discipline (Section 5) and fail-closed principle (Section 7). This is a governance-compatible constraint on the refactor itself.
notes: Code module names like 'layer2/index_suite.py' and import paths must be protected
Historical references preserved for traceability (per CLAUDE.md Section 2.3) must be flagged for governance review, not auto-replaced
series_registry.json entries must not be altered (CLAUDE.md Section 8)

claims.claim_text: Detect whether README_LAYER2.md and any other filenames require rename handling.
claims.classification_rationale: README_LAYER2.md is explicitly named in CLAUDE.md Sections 2.1, 2.2, 2.4, and 11 as a canonical document with a specific declared role. Renaming this file would require updating every cross-reference in CLAUDE.md and the canonical documentation set. This is a current-state concern because the filename is part of the current canonical document identity and authority chain. CLAUDE.md Section 2.2 assigns it a specific canonical role — any rename must preserve that role assignment and all references.
notes: CLAUDE.md references README_LAYER2.md by exact filename in at least 6 locations
The file's canonical role (collaborator guide, Layer-2 build reference) would need role-text updates if renamed
Downstream references in DOCUMENTATION_VERIFICATION_MATRIX_v1.md would also need updates
File rename has high blast radius across the constitutional and canonical document set

claims.claim_text: The refactor must fail closed if it would introduce ambiguity, architecture drift, or snapshot-boundary confusion.
claims.classification_rationale: Directly supported by CLAUDE.md Section 7 (fail-closed principle): 'The system MUST default to NO OUTPUT rather than incorrect output.' Also supported by Section 6 (snapshot contract is non-negotiable) and Section 12 (behavior must be reproducible). The request's fail-closed constraint is a restatement of constitutional principles applied to this specific refactor. This is verified current-state governance.
notes: Fail-closed is a constitutional obligation, not merely a request preference
Snapshot-boundary confusion would violate CLAUDE.md Section 6 (non-negotiable)
Architecture drift would violate CLAUDE.md Section 3 (current vs target separation)

claims.claim_text: The refactor affects CLAUDE.md itself — the constitutional document governing all interpretation and truth hierarchy.
claims.classification_rationale: CLAUDE.md is the highest-priority interpretative authority (per its own preamble). It uses 'Layer 2' and 'Layer 3' extensively in Sections 1, 3, 4, 6, 11, and the stage-gate model. Modifying CLAUDE.md is a contract-affecting change per Section 11, which requires review of all canonical documents. This is a current-state modification to the system's constitutional foundation.
notes: CLAUDE.md Section 11 requires that contract-affecting changes trigger review of all canonical documents
Changing terminology in the constitutional document has cascading governance implications
All downstream interpretation rules reference the layer terminology being changed

claims.claim_text: The proposed terms 'truth_store' and 'decision_layer' are new terminology not currently present in the canonical documentation set.
claims.classification_rationale: The replacement terms 'truth_store' and 'decision_layer' do not appear in CLAUDE.md or in any canonical document title known from the governance context. These are new terms being introduced. Whether they accurately capture the architectural semantics of the existing Layer 2 and Layer 3 concepts cannot be verified from current materials alone — it requires semantic analysis of whether the new names faithfully represent the documented roles without introducing drift. 'truth_store' may be a reasonable semantic match for Layer 2's snapshot-boundary role, but 'decision_layer' for Layer 3 could risk implying decision-making capability that the current system explicitly forbids (CLAUDE.md Section 9: analysis-only, no decision triggering).
notes: 'decision_layer' may conflict with CLAUDE.md Section 9 (execution boundary) and Section 10 (forbidden claims about decisions being automated)
'truth_store' aligns reasonably with Layer 2's role as immutable snapshot boundary, but this is interpretive
Semantic accuracy of replacement terms requires downstream governance review
Risk: 'decision_layer' could be read as implying automated decision capability — needs careful framing

claims.claim_text: The refactor must preserve the distinction between the existing Layer-2 'layer2/index_suite.py' provisional tool and the planned Layer-3 Index Suite component.
claims.classification_rationale: CLAUDE.md Section 3.2 explicitly calls out: 'Index Suite (Layer-3 snapshot-consuming computation; distinct from the existing Layer-2 layer2/index_suite.py provisional pre-publication tool)'. This distinction is a verified current-state architectural boundary. Any rename that conflates these two would violate current-state truth and the current-vs-target separation principle.
notes: The code path layer2/index_suite.py must not be renamed as part of a documentation terminology refactor
The planned Index Suite is target-state; the existing tool is current-state — rename must not merge these identities
